newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, except for gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, except for gold.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures managed a higher close Thursday, with the exception of gold which continued to prove the weakest link in the complex.

"Volume picked up late in the day in gold, with some of the funds which had been covering shorts in August gold recently, starting to re-establish them in the December contract," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said.

COMEX December gold ended down $2.00 at $328.60 an ounce, with the precious metal trading in increasingly narrower ranges in the past 10 days, after recovering partially from 12 year lows in the bullion market around $314.60 in early July.
Estimated COMEX gold volume Thursday was 42,000 lots, well down on activity in the past week.

COMEX gold open interest is also down sharply of late, falling 6,329 lots Wednesday to 188,390 contracts, its lowest level in a month, as funds reduced the record net short positions built up in June.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $324.30/80, compared with the London Thursday afternoon fix at $326.35 and the New York close Wednesday at $325.80/30.
Implied gold lease rates slid further Thursday to around 1.52 percent for one month, from 1.63 pct Wednesday and 1.83 pct Tuesday, suggesting fund borrowing to fund short positions was waning.
But there was little encouragement for the gold market in the latest U.S. economic data Thursday.

While U.S. weekly jobless insurance claims fell to their lowest levels since 1974 in the week ended July 26, the U.S. second quarter GDP price deflator rose only 1.4 pct, the smallest gain since the second quarter 1964.

"Further price weakness in expected for the gold market in the third quarter, with the seasonal slowdown in fabrication demand adding to already very negative market sentiment," Smith Barney analyst David Rinehimer said.
"In the third quarter, we expect a test of the $300 level for the nearby futures," he said.
"Moderate price improvement associated with traditionally stronger seasonal demand and cutbacks in mine production due to unprofitable price levels are expected by the fourth quarter."

In news Thursday the central bank of Lithuania said it was considering selling some of its gold reserves in the future, but Lithuania only held total gold and foreign currency reserves valued at $939.60 million at the end of June, of which only $62.1 million was gold.

Meanwhile, COMEX September silver ended up 11.7 cents at $4.490 an ounce, after breaking out of a $4.20-4.40 range of the past three weeks. Estimated final COMEX silver volume was 20,000 lots, slightly higher than recent daily volume.
Earlier this month spot silver saw three year lows around $4.20 an ounce.

"We continue to feel that downside potential for the nearby (silver) futures will be limited by another global supply deficit and continued good import demand from the U.S., Japan and India," Rinehimer said.

U.S. silver imports rose 12 percent to 547 tonnes in the January-April period this year compared to the same period last year, while Japanese silver imports rose 33 pct to 602 tonnes in the January-May period this year compared to the same period last year.
NYMEX October platinum ended up $1.10 an ounce at $425.50, after seeing a new contract high at $434.00 early.
The October NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread ended at a new high for the contracts at $99.00 an ounce, after climbing over $100.00 an ounce intraday.
NYMEX September palladium closed up $2.60 at $200.60 an ounce, after seeing a new life-of-contract high at $203.00.

No further Russian shipments of platinum group metals (PGMs) are expected in Japan, under the annual supply contract, until August 6, and daily offerings of only about 15,000 ounces of platinum in the spot market by Russia are not meeting demand, traders said.
Russian exports of PGMs resumed in July after a six months suspension. Russia supplies about 20 percent of the world's platinum and 60 percent of its palladium.
